CreateOAuth2Token.name: CreateOAuth2Token
CreateOAuth2Token.documentation: Exchanges an authorization code or refresh token for an OAuth 2.0 access token and refresh token.

CreateOAuth2TokenWithIAM.name: CreateOAuth2TokenWithIAM
CreateOAuth2TokenWithIAM.documentation: Exchanges client credentials for an OAuth 2.0 access token scoped to a resource, which you can use to access AWS services from applications.

CreateOAuth2TokenWithTokenExchange.name: CreateOAuth2TokenWithTokenExchange
CreateOAuth2TokenWithTokenExchange.documentation: Exchanges a supported token for an OAuth 2.0 access token scoped to a resource, which you can use to access AWS services from applications.

DeleteConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration.name: DeleteConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration
DeleteConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration.documentation: Delete console authorization configuration with automatic scope detection

DeleteResourcePermissionStatement.name: DeleteResourcePermissionStatement
DeleteResourcePermissionStatement.documentation: Remove a permission statement from the account's SignIn resource-based policy

GetConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration.name: GetConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration
GetConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration.documentation: Get console authorization configuration with automatic scope detection

GetResourcePolicy.name: GetResourcePolicy
GetResourcePolicy.documentation: Retrieve the account's consolidated SignIn resource-based policy

IntrospectOAuth2TokenWithIAM.name: IntrospectOAuth2TokenWithIAM
IntrospectOAuth2TokenWithIAM.documentation:
Inspects the metadata and active state of an OAuth 2.0 access token or refresh token.

Implements RFC 7662 OAuth 2.0 Token Introspection over a SigV4-authenticated endpoint. Returns the claims associated with a token issued by AWS Sign-In.

ListResourcePermissionStatements.name: ListResourcePermissionStatements
ListResourcePermissionStatements.documentation: Retrieve all permission statements in the account's SignIn resource-based policy

PutConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration.name: PutConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration
PutConsoleAuthorizationConfiguration.documentation: Enable console authorization configuration with automatic scope detection

PutResourcePermissionStatement.name: PutResourcePermissionStatement
PutResourcePermissionStatement.documentation: Create a permission statement in the account's SignIn resource-based policy

RevokeOAuth2TokenWithIAM.name: RevokeOAuth2TokenWithIAM
RevokeOAuth2TokenWithIAM.documentation: Revokes an OAuth 2.0 refresh token and its associated token chain.

error.documentation: One of TOKEN_EXPIRED, AUTHCODE_EXPIRED, USER_CREDENTIALS_CHANGED, or INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS.

AccessDeniedException.documentation: You do not have sufficient access to perform this action.

accessKeyId.documentation: The AWS access key ID for the temporary credentials.

secretAccessKey.documentation: The AWS secret access key used to sign requests.

sessionToken.documentation: The session token that validates the temporary security credentials.

AccessToken.documentation: Contains the scoped, temporary AWS credentials used to sign requests with SigV4. Valid for 15 minutes.

AuthorizationCode.documentation: Authorization code received from AWS Sign-In. Used only in the authorization code redemption flow.

BearerTokenType.documentation: Token type for access tokens. Currently supports "Bearer" as defined in RFC 6749.

CodeVerifier.documentation: PKCE code verifier used to prove possession of the original code challenge. Must be 43 to 128 characters.

error.documentation: OAuth 2.0 error code indicating conflict Will be CONFLICT

message.documentation: Detailed message explaining the conflict Provides specific information about what caused the conflict

ConflictException.documentation:
Error thrown when request conflicts with current state

HTTP Status Code: 409 Conflict

Used when the request conflicts with the current state of the resource

ConsolePermissionMaxResults.documentation: Maximum number of results for list operations

tokenInput.documentation: Flattened token operation inputs. The "grant_type" in the request body determines the specific operation.

CreateOAuth2TokenRequest.documentation:
Input structure for CreateOAuth2Token operation

Contains flattened token operation inputs for both authorization code and refresh token flows. The operation type is determined by the grant_type parameter in the request body.

clientId.documentation: The OAuth 2.0 client identifier. Expected values: "arn:aws:signin:::devtools/same-device" or "arn:aws:signin:::devtools/cross-device".

grantType.documentation:
The OAuth 2.0 grant type. Supported values:

  • "authorization_code" - Exchange an authorization code for tokens.
  • "refresh_token" - Use a refresh token to obtain a new access token.

code.documentation: The authorization code received from the "/v1/authorize" endpoint. Required when "grant_type=authorization_code".

redirectUri.documentation: The redirect URI that was used in the original authorization request. Must match exactly. Required when "grant_type=authorization_code".

codeVerifier.documentation: The PKCE code verifier that proves possession of the original code challenge. Required when "grant_type=authorization_code".

refreshToken.documentation: The refresh token issued by a previous token response. Required when "grant_type=refresh_token".

CreateOAuth2TokenRequestBody.documentation: The request body for creating an OAuth 2.0 token. Supports both the authorization code and refresh token flows, selected by the "grant_type" parameter.

tokenOutput.documentation: Flattened token operation outputs. The specific response fields depend on the grant_type used in the request.

CreateOAuth2TokenResponse.documentation:
Output structure for CreateOAuth2Token operation

Contains flattened token operation outputs for both authorization code and refresh token flows. The response content depends on the grant_type from the original request.

accessToken.documentation: The access token issued by the authorization server. The token contains temporary AWS security credentials that you use to sign requests with SigV4.

tokenType.documentation: The type of token issued. Value is "aws_sigv4".

expiresIn.documentation: The number of seconds until the access token expires. Maximum value is 900 seconds (15 minutes).

refreshToken.documentation: A refresh token that can be used to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating.

idToken.documentation: A JSON Web Token (JWT) containing user identity claims. Present only when "grant_type=authorization_code". Not included in refresh token responses.

CreateOAuth2TokenResponseBody.documentation: The response body for an OAuth 2.0 token request. The fields returned depend on the "grant_type". The authorization code flow returns "refresh_token" and "id_token". The refresh token flow omits "id_token".

resource.documentation: The OAuth resource for which the access token is requested. Example: "aws-mcp.amazonaws.com".

accessToken.documentation: Access token containing principal identity, resource scope, and session metadata.

tokenType.documentation: The token type. Always "Bearer" as defined in RFC 6749.

expiresIn.documentation: Token lifetime in seconds. Value is the minimum of the caller's session validity and 1 hour (3600 seconds).

CreateOAuth2TokenWithIAMResponse.documentation:
Output structure for CreateOAuth2TokenWithIAM operation

Contains the access token, token type, and expiration as defined in RFC 6749 §5.1.

grantType.documentation: The OAuth 2.0 grant type. Currently only supports "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange".

subjectToken.documentation: The subject token that represents the identity of the party on whose behalf the request is made. Required when "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange".

subjectTokenType.documentation: The token type of the subject token. Currently only supports "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt". Required when "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange".

resource.documentation: The OAuth resource for which the access token is requested. Required when "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange". Example: "glue.amazonaws.com".

scope.documentation: IAM managed policy Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) to apply as session policies that further scope down the permissions of the issued access token, provided as a space-delimited list. Example: "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:policy/MyPolicy".

accessToken.documentation: Access token containing principal identity, resource scope, and session metadata.

issuedTokenType.documentation: The token type of the issued token. Always "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token" as defined in RFC 8693 §2.2.1.

tokenType.documentation: The token type. Currently only supports "Bearer" as defined in RFC 6749.

expiresIn.documentation: Token lifetime in seconds. Value is the minimum of the subject token's validity and 1 hour (3600 seconds).

CreateOAuth2TokenWithTokenExchangeRespon.documentation:
Output structure for CreateOAuth2TokenWithTokenExchange operation.

Contains the access token, issued token type, token type, and expiration as defined in RFC 6749 §5.1 and RFC 8693 §2.2.1.

statementId.documentation: Unique identifier of the permission statement to delete

ExpiresIn.documentation: Time to expiry in seconds. At most 900 (15 minutes).

GrantType.documentation: The OAuth 2.0 grant type. "authorization_code" for authorization code redemption, "refresh_token" for token refresh.

IdToken.documentation: ID token (JWT) containing user identity claims. Returned only for authorization code redemption.

InternalServerException.documentation: The request failed because of an internal server error.

token.documentation: The access token or refresh token issued by AWS Sign-In.

tokenTypeHint.documentation: An optional hint about the type of the token submitted for introspection, as defined in RFC 7662 §2.1. The server checks both token types regardless of the hint. Allowed values: "access_token", "refresh_token".

IntrospectOAuth2TokenWithIAMRequest.documentation:
Input structure for IntrospectOAuth2TokenWithIAM operation

RFC 7662 §2.1 introspection request. Contains the token to inspect and an optional hint about the token's type.

active.documentation: Indicates whether the token is currently active. Returns "true" only when the token is valid, has not expired, has not been revoked, and belongs to the caller's account.

clientId.documentation: Client identifier for the OAuth 2.0 client that requested the token.

userId.documentation: User identifier matching the "UserId" field from "sts:GetCallerIdentity" for the token's subject principal.

tokenType.documentation: Indicates which kind of token was introspected. One of "access_token" or "refresh_token".

exp.documentation: Token expiration time as a NumericDate (Unix epoch seconds).

iat.documentation: Token issuance time as a NumericDate (Unix epoch seconds).

nbf.documentation: Token "not before" time as a NumericDate (Unix epoch seconds).

sub.documentation: The IAM principal Amazon Resource Name (ARN). For assumed-role sessions, this is the session ARN.

aud.documentation: The OAuth resource the token is scoped to. Omitted for refresh tokens. Example: "aws-mcp.amazonaws.com".

iss.documentation: Issuer of the token. Always "signin.amazonaws.com" for AWS Sign-In.

accountId.documentation: 12-digit AWS account ID of the token's subject principal.

signinSession.documentation: AWS Sign-In session ARN bound to the token, of the form arn:aws:signin:{region}:{account}:session/{uuid}.

resource.documentation: The OAuth resource the token is scoped to. Only present for refresh token introspection.

IntrospectOAuth2TokenWithIAMResponse.documentation:
Output structure for IntrospectOAuth2TokenWithIAM operation

RFC 7662 §2.2 introspection response. Only active is required; all other claims are omitted when the token is inactive.

IntrospectedTokenType.documentation: The token_type value in the introspection response.

IntrospectionToken.documentation: Token string submitted for introspection. May be an AWS Sign-In access token or refresh token.

InvalidGrantException.documentation: The request failed because the provided grant is invalid or expired.

InvalidScopeException.documentation: The request failed because the requested scope is invalid or exceeds the scope that can be granted.

OAuth2ErrorCode.documentation:
OAuth 2.0 error codes returned by the server

Standard OAuth 2.0 error codes used in error responses to indicate the specific type of error that occurred during token operations.

OAuthAccessToken.documentation: OAuth 2.0 access token containing principal identity and resource scope.

PolicyStatement.documentation: Individual policy statement within a resource-based policy

requestedRegion.documentation: AWS region where the VPC and VPC endpoint reside Required when sourceVpc or signinSourceVpce/consoleSourceVpce is provided

excludedPrincipal.documentation: Principal to exclude from the permission statement

statementId.documentation: Unique identifier for the created permission statement

RedirectUri.documentation: The redirect URI from the authorization request. Must match the original request exactly.

RefreshToken.documentation: The refresh token returned from authorization code redemption. Used in subsequent token refresh requests.

RequestedRegion.documentation: AWS region identifier for VPC and VPC endpoint pairing

error.documentation: OAuth 2.0 error code indicating resource not found Will be RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND

message.documentation: Detailed message explaining which resource was not found Provides specific information about the missing resource

ResourceNotFoundException.documentation:
Error thrown when requested resource is not found

HTTP Status Code: 404 Not Found

Used when the specified resource does not exist

token.documentation: The refresh token to revoke. Must be a refresh token issued by AWS Sign-In. Access tokens are not accepted for revocation.

RevokeOAuth2TokenWithIAMRequest.documentation:
Input structure for RevokeOAuth2TokenWithIAM operation

RFC 7009 §2.1 revocation request. Contains the refresh_token to revoke.

RevokeOAuth2TokenWithIAMResponse.documentation:
Output structure for RevokeOAuth2TokenWithIAM operation

RFC 7009 §2.2 revocation response. The endpoint returns 200 OK with an empty body on success; there are no response fields.

error.documentation: OAuth 2.0 error code indicating service quota exceeded Will be SERVICE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED

message.documentation: Detailed message explaining which quota was exceeded Provides specific information about the limit and current usage

ServiceQuotaExceededException.documentation:
Error thrown when service quota is exceeded

HTTP Status Code: 402 Payment Required (used as quota exceeded indicator)

Used when the request would cause a service quota to be exceeded

ServiceUnavailableException.documentation: The request failed because a dependency is temporarily unavailable. You can retry the request.

TokenExpiresIn.documentation: Token lifetime in seconds. The lesser of session validity and 3600 (1 hour).

TokenType.documentation: The token type. "aws_sigv4" indicates the client must use the token to generate a SigV4 signature.

TokenTypeHint.documentation: Optional token_type_hint value, as defined in RFC 7662 §2.1. One of "access_token" or "refresh_token".

TooManyRequestsError.documentation: The request failed because you exceeded the request rate limit for this operation.

error.documentation: The specific code depends on which validation failed.

ValidationException.documentation: The request failed because it contains a malformed, missing, or invalid parameter.

documentation: AWS Sign-In manages authentication for AWS services. It implements OAuth 2.0, providing secure token exchange and refresh capabilities.
